module_mood_contract: grounded competence — "I can feel when a plan is good before approving it, and I know the move is two reads, not one"
teaching_moment_lands: PASS. Widened to the audience triangle (mid-layer competent, opinionated senior, fast operator), all anchored on the AE101 base persona. The first read produces two concrete push-backs without exhaustive recall, and the second read applies deliberately stronger pressure while leaving selection, steering, and stopping with the reader. The mid-layer and fast-operator traces score 8 across every teaching beat. The opinionated senior — the persona most likely to believe 'two push-backs then a second agent read' is already their habit — dips to 7 at Phase 3 (the forced two-push-back quota reads as manufactured critique on a plan they'd defend as tight, and the in-body text doesn't offer the defend-per-axis escape the trainer-facing Watch-fors section does) but recovers to 8 at Phase 4, where the walk-down's systematic branch walk surfaces a dependency their own habitual pass missed — that recovery is the genuine finding: the exercise does show a strong senior something their existing two-read habit doesn't already deliver, but it does so via Phase 4's mechanics, not via anything Phase 3 tells them. See `personas` array below for per-persona scores; the three do not average to one number, they disagree at exactly the beat the task asked to watch. This fire re-verifies the file after the 2026-08-12 cut of the pre-action `**What happened:**` recap block (commit 3683596, 'a re-narrating What-happened block in push-back-on-the-plan'): the block sat between 'Compare what each read caught' and the maintainer fence, restated the just-run beat in past tense, and its closing clause ('the gap between the two reads is on the record') asserted a persisted artifact the exercise does not produce — Phase 5 is discussion only, nothing new is written to disk. Its removal is correct and is not proposed for restoration.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No pair, group, room-share, or trainer-authored conversation cue anywhere in the body. Move-on and timebox language (lines 62, 73, 79, 91) governs the individual engineer's own working memory, not cohort management.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test names three observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer 'Leap test (Monday)' block (lines 234-237) names three observable own-codebase actions: picks plan mode before approving a multi-file change, sends two specific push-backs naming step numbers before approving a non-trivial plan, runs a second-pass walk-down on any plan touching more than two files. Each is a named verb, not an abstract competency.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each phase with a forcing function has a maintainer failure mode and escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived per phase against current line numbers. P1's no-task failure has the three-candidate recovery (Push-back moves, line 221). The P2/P3 read-and-push-back sequence has diagnostics and escapes for rubber-stamping, performative critique, re-softening, timer abuse, and senior refusal (Watch-fors, lines 200-204; Push-back moves, lines 222-225). P4's failure mode is over-answering after the walk-down stops changing the plan (Watch-fors, line 205) paired with the trainer move at Push-back moves line 226. P5 deflection has its diagnostic and probe at Watch-fors line 206. No phase with a forcing function is left without both a named failure mode and a recovery move. Persona-triangulation (opinionated senior) confirms the design is intentional but facilitator-dependent: the rule asks for a maintainer escape hatch, and the P3 senior-refusal move is exactly that — trainer-facing, not student-facing — which is why the senior persona's P3 mood lands at 7 (facilitator-premium signature) rather than 8 in a self-paced read. Compliant with the rule as written; not a REVISE.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Confirmed clean at current HEAD. Every fenced prompt's lead-in names activity or artifact-contract, never the reveal (lines 27-28 name the drop-in slot; lines 64-69 name the walk-down mechanism, not its findings; line 111 asks a question rather than answering it). The pre-action `**What happened:**` block that violated this rule ('the gap between the two reads is on the record') was cut on 2026-08-12 (commit 3683596) and is not restored here; the exercise's only reflection now lands post-action in 'Compare what each read caught', which is the correct location per this rule and per the maintainer note at line 134.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named and honored; mood floor applies to teaching beats only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Triangulated trace: mid-layer-competent and fast-operator personas score 8 at every teaching beat and 8 at close; Phase 1 is correctly mood-exempt setup for all three. The opinionated-senior persona dips to 7 at P3 (still above the <7 REVISE floor — facilitator-premium signature, not a violation) and recovers to 8 at P4 and close. No persona falls below 7 at any beat, so the floor holds across the triangle, not just the base case. The leave-state for all three is grounded competence: each can allocate attention, cut depth, and approve on judgement rather than coverage. Removing the recap block does not touch any teaching beat's mood, since the block sat after the last teaching beat and inside a strictly bookkeeping position.

Push-back and re-softening are framed as craft ('the discipline stays with you after approval too', line 37) not failure-avoidance. The cut recap block's tone was neutral-summary rather than punitive, so its removal has no bearing here; the file was already clean on this axis.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: What-you-do (line 5) and What-you-build (line 7) open on the two-read discipline itself, not on a plan-mode failure to avoid. Unaffected by the recap-block cut, which sat at the close, not the open.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity: front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood doesn't resolve early, all consolidated.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The exercise runs the strategy doc's core-exercise sequence intact (task pick, plan-mode read, two push-backs via keep-planning-with-feedback, walk-down grill inlined without front-running M3's skill reveal, approve-and-stop, name-the-pattern retrospective) and does not resolve M3's earned-trust mood early — Phase 5 explicitly stays at recognition, never touches execution. The third push-back axis is named 'Alternatives' rather than the strategy doc's 'committed change'; the file's own maintainer block (line 130) documents this as an Antti-directed rename to avoid a collision with 'commit' as a git term elsewhere in the arc, so it is a deliberate divergence, not drift. The removed recap block's overclaim ('the gap between the two reads is on the record') would have misstated the module's actual close (in-chat naming, no persisted comparison artifact) against the strategy doc's own close description; cutting it restores fidelity rather than breaking it.
